ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) domestic designations, the United Nations Act 1946 sanctions regulations, and the Russia Sanctions Act 2022; OFAC SDN List and UK/EU consolidated sanctions lists are additionally screened as institutional best practice. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, must be identified under FATF Recommendation 12 and subjected to enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring proportionate to the low-risk executive headhunting business model.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – New Companies Register and NZBN Name Reservation Portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Roman characters compatible with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register; English is the operating statutory language. Te Reo Māori words and diacritics (e.g., macrons) are accepted, but the name must be reproducible in the ASCII-encoded Companies Office registry and must not be misleading, offensive, or likely to create confusion with an existing registered name. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (unless an approved exemption applies) and may not contain characters other than letters A–Z, numerals 0–9, spaces, and limited punctuation such as hyphen, ampersand, apostrophe, comma, or period.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the New Zealand Companies Office within 20 working days of the notice, citing the original name request reference and submitting legal grounds addressing the Registrar's objection under section 24 of the Companies Act 1993. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file an alternative name request simultaneously or pursue judicial review of the Registrar's decision in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. Extensions of a previously reserved name are available for an additional statutory fee; no extension is available after the reservation period has lapsed without application for incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible for the New Zealand registered office of an International Company, provided the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address within New Zealand, accepts service of legal process and statutory documents, and provides mail forwarding and document handling. For a white-collar, low-risk ISIC 7830 executive search and headhunting agency, the virtual office does not by itself trigger adverse tax-residency or commercial substance challenges, but the New Zealand Companies Office must have accurate consent records and the registered agent must maintain effective communication channels. The tax-exempt international company classification further requires that all business operations remain non-resident sourced and that no domestic New Zealand-source income is derived.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 5% annual likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk executive headhunting agency under the AML/CFT supervisory framework; the likelihood may increase to approximately 15% if the registered agent is a high-volume corporate service provider, if wire retainer flows originate from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions, or if inconsistencies arise in UBO declarations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss. 10-16, 39-42, 88, 128-130, 189-191; Companies (General Matters) Regulations 1995 (New Zealand); Financial Reporting Act 2013; Business Law Reform Act 2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Office Form 2) filed electronically through the Companies Office online incorporation portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Companies Act 1993. Shares may be issued for nil or nominal consideration provided the shareholders agree. No escrow or capital deposit is required for a private company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED duly adopted by the Sole Director in accordance with section 190 of the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) on [DATE]. WHEREAS: (A) The Company was duly incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 and is registered with the New Zealand Companies Office under registration number [NUMBER]; (B) the principal business of the Company is the provision of C-suite executive search, specialist technology headhunting, and talent advisory services; and (C) the directors intend to establish the corporate and operational governance framework. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The proposed allotment of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value is approved. The subscribers named in the share application are hereby allotted shares in accordance with the subscription agreement, and the consideration declared in the statutory register is accepted in full satisfaction of the Companies Act capital rules. Share certificates shall be executed under the Common Seal or under hand of the director and delivered to each shareholder. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company shall be maintained at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], New Zealand, and notification thereof shall be lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office in compliance with section 189 of the Companies Act 1993. The director is authorised to change the registered office and update the address for service as necessary for proper corporate administration. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [NAME] is hereby appointed as sole director, and [NAME] is appointed as Chief Executive Officer; [NAME] may additionally serve as Company Secretary if so agreed. Each officer shall have authority to sign contracts, open and operate bank accounts, execute electronic payment instructions, and represent the Company before regulators within the limits set by the Constitution. 4. BANKING AND PAYMENT RAILS: The opening of a New Zealand dollar corporate account and a Wise B2B multi-currency account is approved. The director and the Chief Executive Officer are named as authorised signatories; any payment exceeding [AMOUNT] must be approved by two authorised signatories. 5. STATUTORY LICENSING: The director is authorised to obtain and maintain any required occupational or industry authorizations, including Immigration New Zealand Accredited Employer certification where necessary, and to engage with the local territorial authority for building, health and safety, and fire clearances. 6. CORPORATE RECORDS: The statutory registers of shareholders, directors, and charges shall be established and maintained at the registered office. The director is authorised to file all annual returns and financial statements with the Companies Office and Inland Revenue in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013. 7. ADOPTION OF THE CONSTITUTION: The Constitution presented to the board is adopted in its entirety and shall govern the proceedings of the Company unless amended by special resolution in accordance with section 32 of the Companies Act 1993. The first board resolution is passed unanimously by the Sole Director and is effective from [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability and Business Structure Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZBN / Online Name Search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search through the New Zealand Companies Office online register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name or registered trademark. Verify that the suffix 'Limited' is adopted. Confirm the executive search business scope does not fall under any restricted name category. If the entity is to operate as an 'International Company' for cross-border fee receivables, confirm that the proposed name is registrable as an ordinary New Zealand company carrying on international business.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative names
Directors' and shareholders' proposed names and jurisdictions
Authority to reserve within executive search and headhunting industry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the search indicates a reservation failure or name conflict, file a different proposed name or request a name consent from the holder. Where an objection is raised by a third party, discontinue the name and immediately reserve an alternative through the Companies Office online portal. Re-submission within 5 working days is allowed without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Incorporation Documents and Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Online Filing Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the application for incorporation (Form 2) and, if desired, a customised constitution compliant with section 122 of the Companies Act 1993. For a standard executive headhunting agency, the default company constitution is acceptable; a bespoke constitution may include share transfer restrictions and director quorum rules. Obtain and execute directors' consents under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993; if any document is signed outside New Zealand, apply for notarization and apostille pursuant to the Foreign Documents Act 1995. Collect the registered office address and address for service, ensuring it is within New Zealand and physically accessible during business hours.
required_dossiers: Notarized ID and proof of residence for directors/shareholders
Apostilled authority if a non-resident corporate shareholder appoints a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries the constitution or consent forms, amend the document and re-submit via the portal within 10 working days. Where the registered office address is invalid, promptly secure a compliant New Zealand address and file a notice of change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via business.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed incorporation application electronically. Pay the prescribed registration fee using a credit card or online payment method. Upon successful processing, the Companies Office will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Verify that the Company's name, director details, share registry and registered office appear exactly as resolved by the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Consent forms and registered office consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused or ‘notice of intention to refuse’ is issued, correct the deficiencies stated in the notice and file a new application through the Companies Office. Any incorrect director consent can be cured by submitting a fresh consent with stated effective date and integrity verification. The Companies Office generally processes corrected applications within 2 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Inland Revenue (IRD and GST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the NZBN will be shared with Inland Revenue to create a tax file number. Confirm the IRD number in the Companies Office IRD registration. If annual turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000, apply for GST registration either through IRD online services or by completing Form GST 101. If the agency will employ staff, register as an employer with PAYE obligations. Confirm eligibility for any NZ foreign-source or international services tax exemptions applicable to non-resident shareholders under the Income Tax Act 2007, but still maintain mandatory tax record keeping.
required_dossiers: Bank account details for tax refunds
Statement of intended executive search operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue does not automatically create the IRD profile within 5 working days, contact Business Registration Services and provide the NZBN. Where a GST application is queried, file a corrected GST 101 or call IRD to resolve classification mismatches. Tax penalties are avoided by responding to IRD correspondence within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Accredited Employer and Immigration Licensing Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Immigration New Zealand and Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the executive search agency will recruit or sponsor foreign talent. If the agency provides services requiring work visas, apply for Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) accreditation with Immigration New Zealand by completing the online employer accreditation application. Provide evidence of financial capacity, a compliant employment agreement, and commitment to employment standards. If the agency will give immigration advice directly to clients, ensure at least one licensed immigration adviser holds a current licence under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007; otherwise, refer all visa questions to a licensed adviser.
required_dossiers: Company financial statements or bank proof of viability
Sample executive service agreement and employment agreement
AML/KYC documentation for the search agency
Policy statement on ethical recruitment and anti-exploitation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an accreditation decision is declined on the basis of 'potentially prejudicial information', respond in writing within the statutory deadline with financial and operational evidence. An independent appeal may be lodged with immigration authorities where the decision is unreasonable. For council or MBIE licensing queries, provide a remediated assessment plan within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and Corporate Records Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank, Wise B2B, and New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the company's New Zealand dollar bank account and a Wise B2B multi-currency account to receive retainer wire payments and cross-border transactions. Provide beneficial ownership declarations and comply with anti-money laundering verification. Establish the registered office filing system for share register, director register, and charges register. Adopt a board minute book and implement the first board resolution's designated signatory structure. Notify the Companies Office of any address for service or director changes.
required_dossiers: Directors'/beneficial owners' passports and utility bills
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or Wise account application is refused due to AML concerns, submit an enhanced due diligence letter and source-of-funds explanations. Where the Companies Office identifies incomplete registers, update the register and file the necessary changes through the online portal within 5 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) – Employment Relations and Labour Inspectorate; Immigration New Zealand; Local Territorial Authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Accredited Employer Certificate (Accredited Employer Work Visa regime) issued by Immigration New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 and Immigration (Accredited Employer Work Visa) Regulations 2022; where relevant, Immigration Adviser Licence under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007. No separate domestic employment agency licence is required for executive search services conducted in New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand and Local Territorial Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Full EIA Report not required. Executive search and headhunting offices are classified as low-impact commercial activity and typically constitute a permitted activity under District Plan commercial zones. No environmental impact assessment is required absent large-scale construction, unique natural water discharges, or resource consent triggers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous air emissions are generated by office-based executive search services. Any minor office wastewater discharges must comply with the local council trade waste bylaw; general waste must be disposed in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; any accidental discharges of substances must be reported under the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017 if thresholds are exceeded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office premises must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness or a Certificate of Acceptance under the Building Act 2004, including structural load compliance and means-of-escape certification. Fire safety clearance must be obtained through Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) confirming automatic detection, alarm, and evacuation compliance under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. WorkSafe New Zealand clearance includes a documented worker health and safety induction, first aid facilities, electrical safety certificates, and compliance with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for office-based operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake), Government of New Zealand; digital self-service portal 'myIR' at https://www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company (IC) incorporated under the Cook Islands International Companies Act 2012 and administered outside New Zealand is not automatically required to hold a New Zealand IRD number unless it derives New Zealand-source income or elects to register for GST. Procedure for a foreign entity to obtain a statutory TIN/VAT ID: (1) confirm non-resident status by ensuring central management and control is not exercised in New Zealand and no New Zealand permanent establishment exists; (2) if the IC derives New Zealand-source income (e.g., executive search fees for placements in New Zealand or fees sourced to New Zealand), complete Inland Revenue registration forms IR596 (Non-Resident Company Registration) and IR742 (Non-Resident Taxpayer Information) and submit through myIR or by post to Inland Revenue, PO Box 39090, Wellington; (3) for GST purposes, if a GST registration obligation is triggered, file form GST1 via myIR providing the IC's incorporated name, registered agent address in the Cook Islands, proof of incorporation, and details of the New Zealand representative; (4) where the IC has no New Zealand nexus, it must nonetheless obtain a Cook Islands tax exemption certificate under the International Companies Act to evidence its zero-tax status; (5) maintain a New Zealand-approved non-resident contractor withholding tax (NRWT) registration only if NZ-source withholding obligations exist. No minimum capital or physical presence is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: The IC is a non-resident foreign company benefiting from a statutory zero-tax regime in its jurisdiction of incorporation; it is outside the New Zealand corporate income tax net on foreign-sourced executive search and headhunting fees, provided no permanent establishment and no central management and control in New Zealand. Entity_Level_Taxation: The company is a separate legal person and any New Zealand-source income is taxed at the entity level at the corporate rate of 28%; no pass-through treatment is available. Territorial_Scope: New Zealand taxes only income sourced within New Zealand for non-resident companies; offshore fees for C-suite search and tech headhunting services supplied to overseas clients are foreign-sourced and exempt. Pass_Through_Eligible: Not applicable — a non-resident IC is not eligible for New Zealand Look-Through Company (LTC) status, which is restricted to NZ-resident close companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime and does not permit unilateral hybrid entity elections. Available mechanisms for a non-resident IC: (1) selection of tax residence through governance — avoiding central management and control in New Zealand; (2) application of a double tax agreement (e.g., NZ–Cook Islands limited treaty network or applicable tie-breaker rules) to claim non-resident status and relief from NZ taxation; (3) the hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 may apply to deny deductions in New Zealand if the IC's zero-tax status creates a hybrid mismatch with an NZ payor; the IC may, however, elect to align its tax characterisation under the OECD Hybrids Tool and provide substantiation to the counterparty; (4) election to register for GST on a voluntary basis even if below the threshold, to claim input credits on NZ expenses; (5) no LTC election available for the IC as a non-resident company; no check-the-box election is available in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 annual taxable turnover for supplies made from a New Zealand fixed establishment or in the course of a New Zealand taxable activity; NZD 130,000 annual threshold for suppliers of remote services (cross-border digital and offshore services) to New Zealand-resident consumers. Executive search and headhunting services supplied by a Cook Islands IC to overseas clients are outside the NZ GST net, as the supply is made by a non-resident supplier with no NZ establishment and the recipient is a non-resident. If the IC invoices New Zealand-resident business clients for headhunting services, the NZ client self-assesses GST under the reverse charge mechanism (section 8(4B) of the GST Act), and the IC is not required to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls, and no digital stamping requirement. Inland Revenue does not require API-based clearance of tax invoices prior to issue. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and based on the Peppol framework; government agencies require Peppol-enabled e-invoicing for B2G transactions, but private B2B use is optional. GST returns (GST101) must be filed through myIR on a one-monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly filing cycle, and GST payments are due by the 28th day of the month following the taxable period. For zero-rated exports, the supplier must retain sufficient documentation to substantiate the zero-rating, but no pre-clearance or real-time validation is mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: exports are zero-rated if the supplier exports the goods within 28 days of the time of supply and retains customs documentation proving physical removal from New Zealand. For services: executive search, headhunting, and talent advisory services are zero-rated under section 11(1) of the GST Act where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and the services are not supplied in connection with land in New Zealand or goods situated in New Zealand at the time of supply. Where the IC supplies C-suite executive search and specialist tech headhunting services to a foreign corporate client (offshore retainer and success-fee model), the supply qualifies for 0% GST provided the client is not resident in New Zealand and is outside New Zealand when the service is performed; the IC must obtain and retain written evidence of the client's non-resident status, the export service contract, dated invoices, and bank receipts of inbound remittance in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Trade Single Window lodgement) — applicable if goods are exported as part of the supply
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from New Zealand within 28 days of supply
Inward Remittance Certificate from the New Zealand bank showing receipt of export proceeds from the overseas client
Fully executed executive search and headhunting services agreement identifying the non-resident client and the offshore nature of the engagement
Dated zero-rated tax invoice (GST 11) issued by the IC to the overseas client
Certificate or official documentary evidence of the client's non-resident tax status (e.g., foreign tax registration, certificate of incorporation, or board resolution confirming offshore location)
Bank statements / Wise B2B transaction records evidencing receipt of retainer wire payments and success fees from overseas
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue actively audits export zero-rating claims under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and the Tax Administration Act 1994. If a zero-rating claim is found to be unsupported by the required documentary evidence, or if the supply is ultimately determined to be taxable, the IC is liable for the shortfall in GST output tax at 15%, plus use-of-money interest calculated from the original due date. Shortfall penalties escalate by culpability: 20% for failing to take reasonable care, 40% for an unacceptable tax position, 100% for gross carelessness, and 150% for fraudulent intent or evasion. In addition, late payment penalties accrue at 1% per month (plus an initial 10% penalty on the 7th day after the due date and a further 10% on the 30th day). Fraudulent zero-rating or deliberate misrepresentation exposing export documentation is a criminal offence under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, punishable by fines of up to NZD 250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; directors of the IC may also be pursued personally for knowingly filing false returns. Where the IC has issued a GST refund claim based on exported services and the claim is clawed back, Inland Revenue may also impose a further statutory interest charge and, for repeated non-compliance, seek an order for tax pooling arrangements or compulsory deregistration of the GST number.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), acting in coordination with the Financial Markets Authority and the Department of Internal Affairs under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully convertible currency under a floating exchange rate regime. There are no exchange controls restricting current account or capital account transactions, and no prior regulatory approval is required for profit remittance, dividend distribution, or liquidation repatriation. Non-resident shareholders may freely repatriate lawful profits after satisfying the applicable Companies Act solvency and distribution tests, bank AML/KYC and beneficial ownership verification, and any tax clearance requirements. Practical hurdles are limited to documentary due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, and bank compliance checks rather than currency convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand does not impose any statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirements on export receipts or service revenues. Exporters and cross-border service providers may retain foreign currency proceeds indefinitely, with no legally mandated conversion ratio, amount, or timeline. Nevertheless, all cross-border payments remain subject to reporting, sanctions screening, AML/CFT customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, and income tax disclosure obligations under New Zealand law.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as a supplementary cross-border disbursement rail for outbound retainer wires and low-value B2B transfers, particularly Wise B2B; Low as a primary treasury account because offshore digital EMIs are not registered banks in New Zealand and cannot provide direct NZD clearing through the Exchange Settlement System. Legal constraints: an offshore EMI must operate only under a valid New Zealand financial service provider arrangement or an equivalent registered-bank exemption, must satisfy AML/CFT Act obligations, and must not hold client funds in a manner that constitutes unregistered bank custody. The CK_IC should maintain at least one fully regulated New Zealand bank account for capital escrow, FX settlement, and high-value transactions, using the EMI solely as a supplementary service-retainer payment channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a standard low-risk New Zealand corporate account, directors are generally not required to appear physically at a branch; banks accept remote onboarding through electronic identity verification, notarised or consular-certified identification, and secure video interviews where the verification process satisfies the AML/CFT Act. For an offshore tax-exempt international company such as the CK_IC, banks commonly impose strengthened conditions: a video or in-person interview with at least one director, a local contact director, certified original identity documents for all beneficial owners, and a bank reference from the funder's home jurisdiction. Remote opening may be approved on a case-by-case basis where the beneficial owner already maintains a substantive relationship with the New Zealand bank and the company's commercial substance, source of funds, and headhunting business model are comprehensively documented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt International Company status without full economic-substance evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and continuance, international company constitution, certificate of good standing, official tax exemption ruling or tax residence certificate, statutory register of shareholders and directors, audited financial statements, and a written commercial-substance memorandum explaining the executive-search revenue model, client relationships, and reason for using the tax-exempt vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and beneficial owners spread across multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially or consularly certified passports and proof of residential address for each director and beneficial owner, AML/CFT-compliant individual due diligence questionnaires, bank reference letters from regulated financial institutions in each source jurisdiction, signed declarations of lawful source of wealth, and detailed biographical information relevant to senior executive search and headhunting integrity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of local New Zealand physical presence or local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office arrangement with a licensed New Zealand service provider, local corporate services agreement showing professional administration, virtual office or co-working access agreement, entity governance documentation (resolutions, accounting records, meeting minutes), and evidence that treasury and client-relationship functions are professionally managed from or through the New Zealand jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for inbound capital injection and shareholder contributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original bank statements of the funding shareholder for at least the preceding six to twelve months, shareholder resolution authorising the capital contribution, loan or subscription agreement, SWIFT payment order linking the remittance to the escrow account, sworn declaration of lawful source of funds, and evidence of tax compliance or tax clearance from the remitting jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume retainer wires and cross-border disbursements through Wise B2B or similar non-bank payment channels
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercially signed executive-search retainer agreements, fee schedules, sample invoices, placed-candidate evidence and placement records, underlying client due diligence files, a treasury policy governing permitted payment rails, and transaction-level reconciliation reports linking each outbound payment to a specific retainer or operational obligation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the shareholder's or investor's regulated bank directly to the CK_IC's New Zealand bank account. New Zealand does not require exchange-control approval, but the remittance narrative must clearly state the economic purpose, e.g., 'equity contribution' or 'subordinated loan for working capital', and must reference the relevant shareholder resolution or finance agreement. The receiving New Zealand bank will conduct source-of-funds verification, sanctions screening, and beneficial ownership review before crediting the capital escrow account. A complete due-diligence pack, including corporate authorisations, constitutional documents, tax status, and funding bank statements, should be forwarded to the relationship manager before the wire is initiated to avoid delay or compliance rejection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for executive-search retainers, operating costs, and candidate onboarding fees should be executed as SWIFT MT103 through the New Zealand banking system. Domestic NZD payments clear through the Exchange Settlement System, while cross-border FX and international payments settle via SWIFT GPI and correspondent banking channels. Commercial letters of credit may be used only for ancillary procurement or trade transactions; service retainers are normally paid by direct MT103 wire transfer. Supporting documentation, including signed retainer agreements, invoices, placement contracts, client KYC records, and beneficial ownership declarations, must be retained to satisfy AML/CFT audits, transaction monitoring, and counterparty sanction screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with New Zealand registered banks
Cross-currency swaps under an ISDA Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on NZD, permissible only in exceptional non-resident contexts or where counterparty credit terms require NDF settlement given the underlying exposure is not otherwise deliverable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: NZ Companies Office Annual Return (Form AR) — statutory confirmation of company name, registered office, address for service, directors and residences, shareholder details, and significant controllers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: filing window opens on the first day of the month of incorporation and closes on the last day of the following month (two-month statutory window); reminder notices issue 20 working days before the window opens
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing places the company in 'annual return overdue' status; the Registrar issues a removal notice and, after publication in the New Zealand Gazette and expiry of 20 working days, strikes the company off under s. 318 of the Companies Act 1993 with all assets vesting in the Crown; each director is liable on conviction to a fine of up to NZ$10,000 (approx. USD 6,200) under s. 211; reinstatement requires a court or Registrar restoration order at substantial cost.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Significant Controller (UBO) confirmation and beneficial ownership statement renewal filed concurrently with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Significant Controllers — New Zealand Companies Office (Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2023)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the Form AR within the anniversary filing window; the internal Register of Significant Controllers must additionally be updated within 10 working days of any notifiable change of control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence-based enforcement: the company is liable on conviction to fines up to NZ$10,000 and each director up to NZ$5,000 for failure to maintain or update the register; any significant controller who fails to comply with a statutory notice faces fines up to NZ$10,000; an incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership confirmation prevents a compliant annual return and supports deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IR4 Annual Company Income Tax Return — filed on a nil / non-resident exempt basis where the International Company derives no New Zealand-sourced income and is not a New Zealand tax resident
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard balance date of 31 March: return due 7 July in the following income year; registered tax-agent extensions may defer the filing date to 31 March of the following income year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NZ$250, increasing to NZ$500 upon continued default; late-payment penalties of 1% per month plus an initial 4% imposition; IRD may issue a default assessment based on estimated income; directors remain personally liable for unpaid withholding or GST obligations, but no corporate income tax liability arises on non-resident offshore income under the tax-exempt status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements — board-approved and signed; audited and filed with the Companies Office only if the 'large company' threshold is crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and Shareholders for approval; New Zealand Companies Office for public filing (large companies only)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be completed and approved within 5 months after the 31 March balance date (by 31 August); large companies must file audited financial statements with the Companies Office within 20 working days of completion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For large companies, each director commits an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for failure to file, with fines on conviction up to NZ$50,000 for the company and NZ$10,000 per director; persistent default constitutes ongoing non-compliance with the Companies Act 1993 and supports strike-off action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit applies only where the International Company qualifies as 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013: total assets exceeding NZ$60 million (approx. USD 36 million) or total revenue exceeding NZ$30 million (approx. USD 18 million), or where the company is an FMC reporting entity or issuer. A small non-resident International Company engaged in executive search and headhunting is below these thresholds and is exempt from mandatory audit; however, shareholders holding at least 5% of the shares or the Registrar may compel an audit, and lender or buyer due diligence covenants may require one commercially.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS (New Zealand equivalents of International Financial Reporting Standards) for large and affected reporting entities; Tier 2 NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR) for entities qualifying for reduced reporting; Simplified Financial Reporting (SPFR) is acceptable for non-reporting small companies for internal, tax, and shareholder purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the board must make reasonable inquiries to identify every significant controller — an individual who owns or controls 25% or more of the shares or voting rights, has the right to appoint or remove a majority of the board of directors, or otherwise exercises significant influence. The Register of Significant Controllers must be updated within 10 working days of any notifiable change, and the beneficial ownership confirmation is delivered to the Companies Office with the Annual Return. The regime applies equally to non-resident international companies, preserving the confidentiality of offshore ownership structures while satisfying UBO transparency obligations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,200 per annum (approx. NZ$850–2,000) for a New Zealand registered office and corporate secretarial/agent service for an International Company
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–8,000 per annum for a voluntary certified audit of a small non-resident International Company (not statutorily required at this size; typically demanded by a lender, buyer, or for tender credibility)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential corporate zones in New Zealand; a resident International Company is taxed at 28% on worldwide income. A temporary reduced rate of 26% applies for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 income years (24% from 2027-28) where net taxable income does not exceed NZD 50,000. The 15% Research and Development Tax Incentive (refundable tax credit, NZD 50,000 expenditure threshold, NZD 150 million annual cap) and the foreign dividend exemption materially reduce the effective rate for qualifying holding structures. Non-resident International Companies are taxed only on New Zealand-source income attributable to a permanent establishment (PE).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry) subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test; where continuity is breached, losses survive only if the same or similar business is carried on for a 5-year period following the breach
